lesson_title: Pap Twice: Maize and the Food Security Riddle
hook_text: Maize is on your plate twice tonight — and you can only see it once.
clip_script: Start at the supper table. Pap, a piece of chicken, maybe an egg on top. Now run the plate backwards like a film. The pap was mealie meal, which was white maize, which stood in a highveld field last summer. The chicken — and the egg — came from birds raised on feed mixed mostly from yellow maize. So maize is on that plate at least twice: once where you can see it, and once hidden inside the chicken. Run the same film for the whole country and you understand why maize outranks its percentages: it is the floor under the national diet.
visual_style: A supper plate rewinding — egg and chicken back to yellow-maize feed, pap back to white maize — landing on a drone sweep over Free State lands and a line of tall silos.
pacing: Warm hook at the table, quick rewind, wide landing on the triangle.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson — the Maize Triangle, two farming worlds, and the full-silos riddle solved.
